workloads.name: Small Files Hierarchy (Initial Sync)
workloads.limitation_notes: Metadata overhead is higher on small files (~350B per envelope); fixed 1MB chunking treats files <1MB as 1 chunk each.

workloads.name: Unchanged Tree Rescan
workloads.description: Re-scanning and synchronizing identical directory with zero modifications
workloads.limitation_notes: Stat-cache optimization eliminates content rehashing; 0 chunk payloads transferred over wire.

workloads.name: Large File Tail Edit (40MB File, 4KB Modified)
workloads.description: Single chunk modification at end of 40MB file
workloads.limitation_notes: 1MB chunking achieves 97.5% bandwidth savings: only Chunk #39 retransmitted; 39 chunks reused from local object store.

workloads.name: Prefix Insertion (1-Byte Offset Shift)
workloads.description: 1 single byte inserted at offset 0 of 20MB file
workloads.limitation_notes: NEGATIVE RESULT: Fixed-size 1 MiB chunk boundaries shift by 1 byte, altering all SHA-256 digests and forcing 100% chunk retransmission (zero chunk reuse). Content-defined chunking (FastCDC/Rabin) is excluded from v1 scope.

workloads.name: File Rename (40MB File)
workloads.limitation_notes: Causal version envelope references existing chunks; content-addressed deduplication renames without transferring any file bytes.

summary: Demonstrates 97.5% - 99.9% bandwidth reduction on tail edits, unchanged scans, and renames, while documenting the negative result of 1-byte prefix shifts on fixed-size chunking.
